long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in an ordinary household in Oegstgeest, Goddijn studied economics and began his career in venture capital. He founded Psion Netherlands, then joined three partners in creating the portable-software business that became TomTom. As chief executive from 2001, he backed the company's move into dedicated navigation devices, including the TomTom GO, and later into automotive mapping and location software.

The transition from consumer hardware to digital mapmaking defined the second half of his leadership. TomTom combined road data, traffic information and software for carmakers, businesses and developers, while Goddijn remained a substantial individual shareholder. He left the chief executive and management-board roles in April 2026 and moved to the supervisory board, separating his continuing governance role from day-to-day management.
